title: An injective abelian sheaf on the small etale site has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for every covering
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $X_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let $\mathcal I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then for every object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ and every covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ of $U$ in $X_{\Et}$ (finite or not), the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex] satisfies $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for all $p>0$. (Stacks states this for any site, together with $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=\mathcal I(U)$, which is not needed here.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech) and its proof: Lemma Tag 03F6 (lemma-injective-abelian-sheaf-injective-presheaf: an injective abelian sheaf is an injective abelian presheaf) and the first part of the proof of Lemma Tag 03AU (lemma-cech-cohomology-derived-presheaves: Hom(Z_{U,.}, I) is the Cech complex, Lemma Tag 03AS, and Z_{U,.} is exact in positive degrees, Lemma Tag 03AT). The module version for Mod(X_et,R) is carried out in steps 1-3 of lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic, through lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact and lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-injective-presheaf; the case R = Z is this statement up to the identification Ab(X_et) = Mod(X_et, Z).

proof.text: Let $\mathcal O=\underline{\mathbf Z}^{p}$ be the constant presheaf of rings on $X_{\Et}$: $\mathcal O(V)=\mathbf Z$ for every object $V$, all restriction maps the identity. A presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (the definition reads verbatim for a presheaf of rings) is a presheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal P$ with a $\mathbf Z$-module structure on each $\mathcal P(V)$ for which the restrictions are $\mathbf Z$-linear; since an abelian group carries exactly one $\mathbf Z$-module structure and every additive map is $\mathbf Z$-linear, the forgetful functor $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)\to\mathrm{PAb}(X_{\Et})$ is an isomorphism of categories, the identity on objects and morphisms. Under it, for an object $V$ the presheaf $\mathcal O_V=\mathcal O[h_V]:W\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\Mor(W,V)}\mathbf Z$ of [lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] is the free abelian presheaf $\mathbf Z_V$ of Stacks, and the complex $K_\bullet=\mathcal O_{\mathcal U,\bullet}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact] built from the covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is Stacks' complex $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal U,\bullet}$ (Lemma 03AS): $K_p=\bigoplus_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}\mathbf Z_{U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}}$ with differential $\sum_j(-1)^j$ times the maps induced by the projections. The fibre products exist in $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AS (lemma-cech-map-into), statement: the complex Z_{U,.} of abelian presheaves

proof.text: The abelian sheaf $\mathcal I$, injective in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], is injective as an object of $\mathrm{PAb}(X_{\Et})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-abelian-sheaf-injective-presheaf], hence, by the previous step, injective in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech), proof, first sentence: Lemma Tag 03F6

proof.text: For every presheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal G$ there is an isomorphism of cochain complexes $\Hom_{\mathrm{PAb}}(K_\bullet,\mathcal G)\cong\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$ [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex], functorial in $\mathcal G$, where the left side has in degree $p$ the group $\Hom(K_p,\mathcal G)$ and differential $s\mapsto s\circ d_{p+1}$. Indeed, a morphism out of a direct sum is a family of morphisms out of the summands, so $\Hom(K_p,\mathcal G)=\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)}\Hom(\mathbf Z_{U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p}},\mathcal G)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] (with the presheaf of rings $\mathcal O$ of the first step) $\Hom(\mathbf Z_V,\mathcal G)\to\mathcal G(V)$, $\beta\mapsto\beta_V(e_{\mathrm{id}_V})$, is a bijection, additive since evaluation is, and natural in $\mathcal G$; so $\Hom(K_p,\mathcal G)\cong\prod\mathcal G(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_p})=\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. For a morphism $g:V'\to V$ and $\beta:\mathbf Z_V\to\mathcal G$ with $\beta_V(e_{\mathrm{id}_V})=s$, the composite $\beta\circ\mathbf Z_g$ sends $e_{\mathrm{id}_{V'}}$ to $\beta_{V'}(e_g)=\mathcal G(g)(s)=s|_{V'}$ (the inverse map of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] is $e_\varphi\mapsto s|_\varphi$); so precomposition with the map induced by the projection omitting the $j$-th factor is restriction along that projection, and precomposition with $d_{p+1}=\sum_j(-1)^j(\ldots)$ is $s\mapsto(\sum_j(-1)^js_{i_0\ldots\hat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_{p+1}}})$, the Cech differential. (This is the module computation of step 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic] for $\mathcal O=\underline{\mathbf Z}^p$; Stacks calls it a tautology.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03AS (lemma-cech-map-into) and its proof (Modules on Sites, Lemma sites-modules-lemma-obvious-adjointness)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact], applied to the presheaf of rings $\mathcal O=\underline{\mathbf Z}^p$ of the first step and the covering $\mathcal U$ (a family of morphisms of $X_{\Et}$ with target $U$), $K_\bullet$ is exact in positive degrees: $H_p(K_\bullet(W))=0$ for every object $W$ and every $p>0$. Since kernels and images in $\mathrm{PAb}(X_{\Et})$ are computed objectwise, this says that for $p>0$ the image of $d_{p+1}:K_{p+1}\to K_p$ equals the kernel of $d_p:K_p\to K_{p-1}$ as subpresheaves of $K_p$.

Let $p>0$ and let $s\in\Hom(K_p,\mathcal I)$ be a cocycle, $s\circ d_{p+1}=0$. Then $s$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}(d_{p+1})=\ker(d_p)$ (previous step), so it factors as $s=t\circ\bar d_p$ with $\bar d_p:K_p\to B=\operatorname{im}(d_p)\subset K_{p-1}$ the corestriction of $d_p$ (an epimorphism with kernel $\ker d_p$, so $B\cong K_p/\ker d_p$) and $t:B\to\mathcal I$. Since $\mathcal I$ is injective in $\mathrm{PAb}(X_{\Et})$ (second step) and $B\to K_{p-1}$ is a monomorphism, $t$ extends to $s':K_{p-1}\to\mathcal I$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and then $s=s'\circ d_p$ is the coboundary of $s'\in\Hom(K_{p-1},\mathcal I)$. Hence $H^p(\Hom(K_\bullet,\mathcal I))=0$ for every $p>0$ (this is exactness of $\Hom(-,\mathcal I)$ applied to $K_\bullet$), and by the third step $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=H^p(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I))=0$ for every $p>0$ [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex].

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 03AW in PAb(X_et), as its source does, rather than through Mod(X_et,Z): the identification Ab(X_et) = Mod(X_et,Z) suggested in the brief is not stated by def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves or def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves and is not elementary (Z_X(V) is the ring of locally constant Z-valued functions, and uniqueness of the module structure needs sheafification), whereas PMod of the constant presheaf of rings Z is PAb identically. Steps: (1) PMod(constant presheaf Z) = PAb, Z_V and K = Z_{U,.} (elementary); (2) I injective in PAb by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-injective-abelian-sheaf-injective-presheaf (Stacks 03F6; Adjunction.map_injective for the sheafification adjunction); (3) Hom(K,G) = Cech complex by lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module (03AS); (4) K exact in positive degrees by lem-weil-pbc-free-cech-complex-exact with O = constant presheaf Z (03AT); (5) Hom(-,I) carries it to an exact complex, written out from the definition of injective. lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-injective-presheaf is not used. Mathlib has no Cech-acyclicity of injective sheaves (Cech.lean defines cechComplexFunctor only); the source repository proves the topological-space analogue TopCat.Presheaf.exactAt_cechComplex_of_injective (sorry-free, finite covers by opens, via Godement sheaves), not this statement.
